const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > docs/quality/summary-qa/ark-nova/2026-11-04-batch-231507/expanded-iteration-01/reader-b.json <<'EOF'
{
  "reader": "reader-b",
  "inputs_read": [
    "/home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules/docs/quality/summary-qa/ark-nova/2026-11-04-batch-231507/expanded-iteration-01/summary-snapshot.md",
    "/home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules/docs/quality/summary-qa/ark-nova/2026-11-04-batch-231507/expanded-iteration-01/questions.json"
  ],
  "answers": [
    {"id":"Q01","answer":"Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active association worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying below it. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards. All five Action cards start side I; Animals goes in the leftmost slot, and the other four are randomized among the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, then 1, 2 and 3 in turn order.","support":"supported","evidence":"Personal setup B–F: Animals card under the leftmost slot; 1 active and 3 lying workers; 25 money; draw 8 and keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; Appeal track staggered by turn order."},
    {"id":"Q02","answer":"The Association setup puts the top 3 Base Conservation Projects face up for 2 or 3 players and the top 4 for 4 players. In a 2-player game, block the left level on the left project, middle level on the middle project, and right level on the right project, plus all three spaces in the donation area's left column. The display's six cards are revealed only after everyone has chosen starting hand cards.","support":"supported","evidence":"Global setup 5b–5c and personal setup G."},
    {"id":"Q03","answer":"After a slot-4 card is used, remove it, shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. Set strength before acting; each X-token spent adds 1 strength, returns to supply, and cannot exceed 5 held. X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect after completing the action, including the card movement.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: ‘set the strength before performing the action’; ‘remove the card from its slot’; ‘shift all Action cards left’; ‘after finishing’ includes moving cards."},
    {"id":"Q04","answer":"You cannot simply do nothing. If you cannot or do not want to take a regular action, select an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; move that card to slot 1 and shift the cards left of its former slot right. Strength and upgrade side do not matter. You cannot take this action while already holding 5 X-tokens.","support":"supported","evidence":"X-TOKEN action (alternative action)."},
    {"id":"Q05","answer":"When the Break token reaches its last space, ignore movement beyond it and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. Finish the current turn, then conduct the break; play resumes clockwise with the next player after the break. The summary does not describe a break itself as granting extra turns; extra turns are part of the separate game-end rule.","support":"supported","evidence":"Break track: ‘break takes place after the end of your current turn’; ‘get 1 X-token’; ‘Ignore any additional steps’; break procedure resets the token and play continues clockwise."},
    {"id":"Q06","answer":"Cards I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck per the card's strength table (up to 3, possibly discarding) or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly 1 display card of any reputation without a deck draw. Cards II also advances 2; draw from the deck and/or from cards within reputation range, in any order, using its table. A side-II snap works at strength 3+ and takes exactly 1 card of any reputation, with no deck draw. Cards II display cards are not replenished until turn end; Cards I snap is also replenished at turn end. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard to the limit only at breaks.","support":"supported","evidence":"CARDS action sides I/II; ‘snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation’; hand limit is checked only at breaks."},
    {"id":"Q07","answer":"Reputation range comprises the display folder matching your Reputation counter and all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action; at reputation 15, each further reputation step instead gives 1 appeal. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.","support":"supported","evidence":"‘Within reputation range’ definition; reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; space 15 overflow; discard pile rule."},
    {"id":"Q08","answer":"Build I builds exactly 1 building of size up to strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, never two identical buildings in one action. Each costs 2 money per space. Your first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by an edge. Build only on empty spaces and not over water or rock; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart. Each pavilion gives 1 appeal when placed.","support":"supported","evidence":"BUILD action, building table and placement rules."},
    {"id":"Q09","answer":"Build I allows standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo per zoo. Build II adds the Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary, also one of each per zoo. The supply has four tiles of each special-enclosure type. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.","support":"supported","evidence":"Buildings available through Build; four tiles of each special enclosure; unique buildings only via Sponsors; full-map rule."},
    {"id":"Q10","answer":"Bonuses gained earlier in an action—including money, cards and newly activated workers—may be used for later steps of that action, but each item must be paid before receiving its own benefits. Immediate effects resolve as they occur; ‘after finishing’ waits until the entire action and Action-card movement are complete. The owning player chooses the order of simultaneous effects.","support":"supported","evidence":"Turn Structure: bonuses gained earlier in an action may be used later; ‘You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits’; simultaneous effects order is chosen by owning player."},
    {"id":"Q11","answer":"For each Animal, meet all left-side conditions and pay its printed cost first. A partner zoo on its continent reduces the cost by 3 per continent icon on that Animal, so two matching icons reduce it by 6. Standard housing requires one empty enclosure at least the required size, then flip the whole enclosure occupied; it normally holds one animal. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Eligible reptiles/birds may instead use a Reptile House/Aviary, marking the indicated number of spaces with supply player tokens; special enclosures never flip and can be shared if capacity remains. Meet any required distinct adjacent water/rock hexes; count hexes, not touching edges. Immediate effects resolve before the next animal; after-finishing effects wait until the Animals action and card movement are complete.","support":"supported","evidence":"ANIMALS action steps 1–5 and ‘Enclosure state on animal admission’; partner discount is 3 money per continent icon."},
    {"id":"Q12","answer":"Animals II may play from hand and from display cards within reputation range, paying the display folder number in addition to the animal's cost. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very start, so the higher range applies immediately. Do not replenish the display until turn end. Animals II also permits Animals cards with the upgrade-required condition.","support":"supported","evidence":"Animals action Side II."},
    {"id":"Q13","answer":"Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move suitable eligible animals into that new enclosure; consider all corresponding animals that fit and decide separately for each. Mark each animal's required number of spaces with supply player tokens, within the five-space capacity. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including terrain; if none does, flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size alone; if none meets size, flip none.","support":"supported","evidence":"‘Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure’ and special-enclosure capacity."},
    {"id":"Q14","answer":"Task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4 and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task; Association II performs one or more different tasks whose total value is no greater than strength. Each task needs an active worker; if one of your workers is already on that task, you must place 2 workers, and if 3 are there you cannot repeat it until after the break. Other players' workers do not matter.","support":"supported","evidence":"ASSOCIATION action, side I, listed task strengths, and side II."},
    {"id":"Q15","answer":"Take partner zoos and universities from the Association board and place them on the lowest available corresponding space of your map; take any printed space bonus immediately, and take a university's printed reputation. You cannot take a duplicate university. Partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4; the third or fourth requires upgraded Association. Universities are the only way to raise hand limit from 3 to 5, and only the hand-limit university does so.","support":"supported","evidence":"Association task descriptions; university table and hand limit."},
    {"id":"Q16","answer":"With Association I, either support a project already in play or play one from hand and support it immediately; Association II also permits playing a new project from the display within reputation range for its folder-number cost. To support, meet an unoccupied condition and place one of your left-edge zoo-map tokens on it. A reward level is unavailable if any player has a token there; each level holds one token total, and normally you may support each project only once. Choose a token from the left edge; its bonus activates immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice. A new project goes leftmost above the Association board, shifting others right; if over the player-count limit (2/3/4), discard the rightmost and return its tokens to owners' supplies. Activated map bonuses remain activated.","support":"supported","evidence":"Conservation project work; two separate support limits; overflow handling."},
    {"id":"Q17","answer":"The animal's printed standard-enclosure size must match the release band: 2− means size 1 or 2, 3 means size 3, and 4+ means size 4 or 5; the occupied tile size/capacity does not set the band. Discard the Animal and lose its printed appeal and icons, but keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. Lose the appeal before gaining project conservation. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. If the animal can live in a special enclosure and its required tokens can be removed, you must remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure satisfying all requirements, or fallback to the smallest meeting size alone, or flip none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies to flock animals too.","support":"supported","evidence":"Release into the wild projects work differently; matching size bands and removal/fallback procedure."},
    {"id":"Q18","answer":"Sponsors I plays exactly 1 card from hand if strength is at least its level and all conditions are met. Sponsors II may play one or more cards if strength +1 is at least their total levels; cards can come from hand or from display within reputation range, paying the folder number extra. Resolve cards sequentially, completing each instant effect before the next; defer after-finishing effects until the action ends. Alternatively, Sponsors I advances the Break token by strength and gives that much money even if fewer spaces remain; Sponsors II gives double that money.","support":"supported","evidence":"SPONSORS action sides I/II."},
    {"id":"Q19","answer":"Break order: discard to hand limit (3, or 5 with hand-limit university); clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide remaining cards down and refill; take income (appeal money, kiosk income, Sponsor/map break income); reset the Break token. Each kiosk earns 1 per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure and pavilion; empty standard enclosures give nothing, empty special enclosures do. For players taking display cards during income, resolve clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.","support":"supported","evidence":"Break procedure steps 1–6 and display-card income ordering."},
    {"id":"Q20","answer":"At 2 conservation, choose an Action-card upgrade or activate an association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or a Bonus token beside that space. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if no one reaches 10, all discard one before scoring. Check the end at the end of your turn or during a break when your Appeal and Conservation counters enter the same scoring area or pass one another; appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn end or a break. If triggered at a turn end, all other players take one more turn; if during a break, all players take one more. Each Final Scoring card can give at most 4 conservation. VP = Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area of your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; tie goes to most project supports, then shared victory.","support":"supported","evidence":"Conservation milestones; End of the game; Final scoring."},
    {"id":"Q21","answer":"At setup, shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place a random one face up on each of the 4 blank yellow Bonus spaces on the board; do not use the two yellow spaces with icons, and return the remaining 5 to the box. At conservation spaces 5 and 8, the summary says to take either 5 money or one Bonus token next to that space, but it does not describe a separate selection/placement procedure for those conservation-track tokens. The summary says to keep some standard enclosures and kiosks/pavilions in reserve and use a suitable substitute if components run out, so the supplied component count is not an absolute limit.","support":"partial","evidence":"Setup: shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place random tiles on four blank spaces; Conservation track 5/8 rewards; Component shortage note."},
    {"id":"Q22","answer":"For advanced maps, either take 2 random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse play order. Map A starts with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on its indicated spaces; place a kiosk tile over its printed kiosk as a reminder.","support":"supported","evidence":"Personal setup A."},
    {"id":"Q23","answer":"The seven player tokens used to support projects start on the designated spaces along the left edge of your zoo map. Hire inactive workers from the lowest reserve space upward. Certain zoo maps grant conservation points when you hire your last worker; the summary does not name a specific map/reward amount for that case.","support":"supported","evidence":"Personal setup C2–C3; Association worker supply edge case."},
    {"id":"Q24","answer":"Flip one chosen Action card from side I to II and leave it in its slot. Its improved action is available from your next action, but it counts as upgraded immediately for conditions. You cannot upgrade all five cards because one of the upgrade opportunities allows an alternative choice.","support":"supported","evidence":"Upgrading Action cards."},
    {"id":"Q25","answer":"Cards I: strength 1 draws 1/discards 1; 2 draws 1/discards 0; 3 draws 2/discards 1; 4 draws 2/discards 0; 5+ draws 3/discards 1. A required discard can be one just drawn or a card already in your hand.","support":"supported","evidence":"Cards draw tables; required discard note."},
    {"id":"Q28","answer":"The seven categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. Bears may also carry herbivore or predator icons but count as a category; Petting Zoo animal is also a category. Include both unless expressly excluded.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base glossary: shared principles; animal categories."},
    {"id":"Q29","answer":"A donation is available only with Association II, after performing at least one Association task in that same action; it needs no worker and is limited to one per Association action. Pay the smallest amount still visible and cover that donation space with a player token from your supply to gain 1 conservation. Costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then a repeatable 12-money space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces except the last are covered, each later donation costs 12 and places no further token.","support":"supported","evidence":"Association II donation rules."},
    {"id":"Q30","answer":"Zoo icons are upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count. A card counts its own icons for effects; doubled icons count twice. Card text takes priority over general rules.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base glossary: card icon counting; ‘Card text takes priority over general rules.’"},
    {"id":"Q31","answer":"Count distinct adjacent water/rock hexes: several edges touching the same hex still count once, and a larger connected water region counts only the hexes actually adjacent. Decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles are neither terrain spaces nor requirements.","support":"supported","evidence":"Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; tile illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements."},
    {"id":"Q32","answer":"Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play gives no extra reputation. Breeding Program projects (123–127) have the same requirement for all three reward levels, so choose any available level.","support":"supported","evidence":"Release into the wild projects; Icon-count projects."},
    {"id":"Q33","answer":"For an effect written X:Y, a condition with no number (or with ‘per’) pays once per fulfillment. A numbered threshold pays only once; if there are several thresholds, use the highest one met.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base glossary: ‘For an effect written “X : Y.”’"},
    {"id":"Q34","answer":"Connected means uncovered and sharing an edge with a covered space. Isolated means no adjacent covered space. A border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply; ‘any zoo’ includes these for all players.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base glossary definitions."},
    {"id":"Q35","answer":"Unique buildings enter through Sponsor cards and must be placed when playing the Sponsor; if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. Use the matching tile, colored face up; rotate freely but do not flip. Follow ordinary placement rules and any terrain requirements, but pay no size-based building cost. Unique buildings are not enclosures and cannot house animals or count as water/rock spaces.","support":"supported","evidence":"Unique buildings must be placed when playing their Sponsor; matching tile/orientation, placement, terrain and cost rules."},
    {"id":"Q36","answer":"After finishing the Animals action and moving its card to slot 1, take the granted action. Use the named Action card normally and move it to slot 1 afterward. A named action cannot be replaced with the X-token alternative; Determination/Any Action may choose the X-token alternative.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base animal ability clarifications: Action / Determination."},
    {"id":"Q37","answer":"Assertion searches the unused face-down base-project deck and adds the chosen card to hand; Dominance does likewise for its named card, but has no effect if that project is already in play. Later play it and support it immediately through Association, placing it above the board, not in the setup base-project row below.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base animal ability clarifications: Assertion / Dominance."},
    {"id":"Q38","answer":"Resolve Boost/Clever after finishing Animals and moving that card. Clever moves the chosen Action card to slot 1, shifting cards formerly to its left right. Boost moves the named card to slot 1 or slot 5; moving it to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base animal ability clarifications: Boost / Clever."},
    {"id":"Q39","answer":"Interactive effects require the affected zoo to have at least 5 appeal. The playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so the new appeal normally need not count when selecting an affected player. The group may use the alternative text marked for solo on interactive cards even in multiplayer. (Pilfering and Hypnosis have their own target-selection rules.)","support":"supported","evidence":"Interactive abilities: five-appeal eligibility, timing of animal appeal and multiplayer option."},
    {"id":"Q40","answer":"Constriction affects other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation: ahead on one track gets 1 token; ahead on both gets 2. Put tokens in highest slots (one on 5, or two on 4 and 5); do not stack two on one card, return duplicates. The action loses 2 strength per relevant Constriction token; each execution of a multiplied action is affected, and X-tokens can restore strength. Return tokens after acting or clear them without effect at the break.","support":"supported","evidence":"Interactive abilities: Constriction."},
    {"id":"Q41","answer":"The summary says that at effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, use the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. Thus a constricted card in slot 1 or 2 cannot be used as a regular action unless strength is restored to at least 1; the X-token alternative is permitted if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens.","support":"supported","evidence":"Constriction: at effective strength zero or below, restore to at least one, use alternative X-token action, or leave card until slot 3 or higher."},
    {"id":"Q42","answer":"Yes. Digging lets you decide again after each card which of the two options to use. If discarding a display card through Digging, replace it immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base animal ability clarifications: Digging 2 / Digging."},
    {"id":"Q43","answer":"A flock animal may avoid a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its standard-enclosure size. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals. Without a qualifying herbivore, house it normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. On release, you need not prove the flock animal's original accommodation: release still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure, even if it shared, and exact historical residents are not tracked.","support":"supported","evidence":"Flock Animal clarification."},
    {"id":"Q44","answer":"Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it to the notepad for immediate use; take any last-worker map reward shown. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.","support":"supported","evidence":"Full-throated clarification."},
    {"id":"Q45","answer":"If no revealed card is an Animal card, discard all revealed cards.","support":"supported","evidence":"Hunter X: ‘With no Animal among them, discard all.’"},
    {"id":"Q46","answer":"For ties at highest appeal, choose the affected player; targeting yourself has no effect. Choose only the target's slot 1, 2 or 3. Use that card's owner's upgraded/unupgraded side for the whole action, but your own X-tokens; move the targeted card to slot 1 normally. Venom and Constriction on it affect you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.","support":"supported","evidence":"Hypnosis rules."},
    {"id":"Q49","answer":"Place a gained Multiplier immediately on its named Action card (a bonus-tile one may go on any card). On its next use, execute the action twice in succession at the same base strength, and move its card only after both. Each X-token boosts only one execution; defer after-finishing effects until both are done. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn is finished. Return used tokens to supply; an unused token is removed at the next break.","support":"supported","evidence":"Multiplier rules."},
    {"id":"Q50","answer":"Two Multiplier tokens allow up to three executions, not four. Each X-token boosts only one execution. A multiplied X-token alternative can take two X-tokens (subject to the five-token cap), but you may not mix an X-token action with a regular action.","support":"supported","evidence":"Multiplier rules: each additional token adds one execution; multiplied X-token alternative."},
    {"id":"Q51","answer":"Peacocking may place a Large Bird Aviary before Build is upgraded, but it still must obey other placement restrictions, including Build II for upgrade-marked map spaces; it fails if you already have that enclosure or no legal site. Posturing follows normal placement rules, including kiosk spacing, and places multiple buildings one at a time.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base animal ability clarifications: Posturing / Peacocking."},
    {"id":"Q52","answer":"The first Petting Zoo animal grants 3 appeal, the second 6, and the third 9. A zoo may have only one Petting Zoo, which holds up to three such animals. Petting Zoo animals count as small animals.","support":"supported","evidence":"Petting Zoo animal clarification."},
    {"id":"Q53","answer":"Pilfering 1 targets the zoo with highest appeal. Pilfering 2 separately targets the zoo with highest appeal and the zoo with most conservation; a conservation leader must have at least 1 conservation point. Ties let you choose the affected player. Self-targeting has no effect.","support":"supported","evidence":"Pilfering X rules."},
    {"id":"Q54","answer":"The target chooses whether to give 5 money or allow a random hand-card draw; Final Scoring cards are never drawn. If the target has no hand cards, they give 5 money; with less than 5 money, they give a card. With neither a card nor 5 money, they give all current money, including zero. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially, and the target may choose differently each time.","support":"supported","evidence":"Pilfering X payment and repeated-resolution rules."},
    {"id":"Q55","answer":"Pouch cards are tucked under the animal, have no remaining function, and earn 2 appeal per card; if the animal is released, discard the tucked cards but keep the appeal already earned. Sunbathing sells up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to the discard pile.","support":"supported","evidence":"Pouch X and Sunbathing X clarifications."},
    {"id":"Q56","answer":"An extra Final Scoring card drawn before the 10-conservation milestone joins the cards from which you discard one at that milestone. At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card, each with its own maximum of 4 conservation points.","support":"supported","evidence":"Resistance clarification."},
    {"id":"Q57","answer":"Shuffle the discard pile face down, draw randomly, make the card's stated selection, then return the discard pile face up. The illustrated Scavenging 3 draws 3 random cards, keeps 1 and discards the others.","support":"supported","evidence":"Scavenging clarification."},
    {"id":"Q58","answer":"Snapping takes exactly 1 display card regardless of reputation; it does not draw from the deck. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsor cards without a reputation-range restriction; if none is present, it has no effect. Ordinary display replenishment occurs at end of turn.","support":"supported","evidence":"Snapping / Sponsor Magnet clarification."},
    {"id":"Q59","answer":"Venom tokens go on cards in the lowest slots (1, then 2, etc.), at most one on each; return duplicates. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn, including using the X-token alternative if you hold fewer than 5 X-tokens. Otherwise, if any Venom remains at turn end, pay 2 money; if unable, undo the turn and choose another action. Unused tokens expire at the next break without effect.","support":"supported","evidence":"Interactive abilities: Venom X."},
    {"id":"Q63","answer":"Veterinarian gives 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities immediately. Its recurring effect reduces Conservation Project work's required strength from 5 to 4. Its final reward is 1 conservation for three universities.","support":"supported","evidence":"Base Sponsor reference, card 203."},
